claims.text: As-cast or homogenized HfNbTaTiZr has a nominal single-phase microstructure.
Exposure of HfNbTaTiZr to elevated temperatures enhances atomic diffusion.
Enhanced atomic diffusion promotes and maintains a stable single-phase solid solution in HfNbTaTiZr.
Stabilization of the single-phase solid solution suppresses dislocation mobility.
Elevated-temperature exposure modulates lattice distortions in the alloy.
Lattice distortions persist at elevated temperatures.
Restricted dislocation motion combined with persistent lattice distortions reduces the thermal expansion coefficient.
The alloy has a lower thermal expansion coefficient at 600–1000°C than at room temperature.
Elevated-temperature diffusion, phase stability, and restricted dislocation motion alter the stress–strain response relative to room temperature.
The altered stress–strain response may include higher yield stress at elevated temperature.
The alloy exhibits enhanced mechanical stability at elevated temperature relative to its room-temperature state.
The proposed mechanism and outcomes hold approximately between 600°C and 1000°C.
The proposed behavior is conditional on the alloy remaining a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The proposed behavior is conditional on the absence of oxidation and secondary-phase changes.
Using moderate strain rates isolates thermal effects on the mechanical response.
Thermal activation is minimal in the room-temperature baseline state.
Relaxation of lattice distortions at elevated temperature may activate slip systems and compete with the proposed stabilizing mechanism.
